.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Showers and thunderstorms this afternoon followed by a strong 
cold front bringing a chance of severe weather Tuesday. 

Temperatures continue to increase today with highs in the upper 70s 
to upper 80s across the forecast area. Southerly flow increases 
humidity as well with a warm and moist air mass yielding increasing 
instability this afternoon. Showers and thunderstorms are 
possible later this afternoon and evening, although coverage 
will be limited due to shortwave ridging aloft.

Showers and perhaps a thunderstorm continue into Tuesday 
morning although recent guidance has chances for AM 
precipitation highest across the northern portions of the 
forecast area. Therefore, SPC has shifted the slight risk for 
severe weather southeast slightly. In the afternoon, 
thunderstorm chances increase ahead of a potent cold front. 
Despite morning precipitation, guidance shows plenty of 
instability across the forecast area which combined with 
strengthening shear leads to an increasing severe weather 
threat. Damaging wind gusts continue to be the primary hazard 
type expected although cooling mid level temperatures yields a 
large hail threat, mainly across the southern portions of the 
forecast area. Additionally, the potent area of surface low 
pressure associated with cold front tracks across the forecast 
area. Where the low pressure system tracks during convective 
activity will yield a brief tornado threat. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Drier conditions anticipated later this week, with increasing 
precipitation chances going into the weekend.

By Thursday, the Great Lakes low will be well off the coast of New 
England as high pressure builds overhead here in the Mid-Atlantic, 
bringing reduced precipitation chances and calmer conditions 
overall. Temperatures will start to gradually increase to the upper 
80s during this period, but drier air aloft will limit heat indices 
increasing beyond the actual air temperature. 

Meanwhile, a broad upper-level trough will begin to form over the 
Ohio River Valley over the weekend. As this trough tracks east, 
cloud cover & precipitation chances will begin to increase, 
particularly between Saturday evening and Sunday as the low tracks 
offshore and towards the northeast. Severe probabilities look 
marginal as of right now, with NCAR's AI ML algorithm only showing a 
low-end 5%-15% probability as of the 00z runs. Nonetheless, weekend 
showers are a potential likelihood with this system should the 
synoptic setup continue to trend toward development over the 
Midwest.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Periods of sub-VFR conditions are possible this evening as showers 
and perhaps a thunderstorm impact the terminals. Prevailing VFR
conditions are expected today with light southerly winds. 
Confidence remains too low for anything more than a PROB30 for 
possible -SHRA in the TAFs for now.

A strong frontal system brings showers and thunderstorms to the 
terminals on Tuesday. Sub-VFR conditions are expected both in the 
morning during rain showers and later in the afternoon as strong to 
severe thunderstorms track across the forecast area. Strong wind 
gusts, low ceilings, reduced visibilities, heavy rain, and frequent 
lightning are all possible in the afternoon. Sub-VFR conditions 
continue into Wednesday morning depending on how slowly the front 
tracks offshore. Winds gust 15 to 25 knots out of the northwest. 

Prevailing VFR conditions are generally anticipated across terminals 
through Thursday and Friday. Winds could still be somewhat gusty on 
Thursday, with 10-15 knot winds gusting up to 20 knots before 
diminishing overnight. Northwest winds begin to shift southerly by 
Friday night. &&

.MARINE...
Southerly winds gust around 15 knots this afternoon. A brief period 
of gusts 15 to 20 knots are possible and will likely be handled with 
an MWS as opposed to a SCA. Winds increase on Tuesday with SCAs 
likely. Active convection will also make for hazardous conditions 
across the waterways. This may include strong winds, abrupt wind 
shifts, and frequent lightning. Winds shift to northwesterly 
overnight into Wednesday with SCA criteria winds likely throughout 
the day. 

SCA conditions remain likely through Thursday, with winds gusting up 
to 20 knots over the waters and flowing northwesterly. Winds 
diminish below SCA thresholds by Friday. &&

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...

Annapolis is forecast to hit minor flood stage during the higher
of the two high tides through Wednesday with other sensitive 
tidal locations reaching action stage.
